title: Prefecture bans all demonstrations in Lyon amid ongoing protests
seoTitle: Lyon protest ban announced amid unrest

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the high cost of living and government policies amid nationwide economic discontent.
tea.want: Demonstrators are calling for action regarding the cost of living through planned protest days.
tea.changed: Oct 22: The Rhône prefecture announced a complete ban on all demonstrations in Lyon for Saturday, 24 October.

summary: Authorities in Lyon announced a total ban on all demonstrations scheduled for Saturday, October 24, following riots and looting that occurred during a nationwide cost-of-living protest the previous week. The Rhône prefecture, representing the state authority overseeing local policing, issued the prohibition as France braced for further unrest under the banner of the "Acte II" protest day called by a Yellow Vest coordination group. The heightened security measures followed weeks of student rallies and cost-of-living demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands nationwide, accompanied by clashes and property damage in several cities. In response to the growing crisis, government officials implemented curfews and demonstration bans across multiple cities.
demands: Address the high cost of living
response: The Rhône prefecture banned all demonstrations in Lyon for Saturday following prior unrest. National authorities also implemented curfews and restricted protests in areas of Paris.

updates.text: Nationwide demonstrations against the cost of living drew hundreds of thousands of participants and were followed by riots.
The Rhône prefecture announced that all demonstrations are banned in Lyon for Saturday, 24 October.
